key_findings: The Transformer reaches 28.4 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-German, more than 2 BLEU above the previous best including ensembles.
It reaches 41.8 BLEU on WMT 2014 English-to-French as a single model.
The big model trains in 3.5 days on eight P100 GPUs, a small fraction of the training cost of competing models.
The architecture uses attention alone, dispensing with recurrence and convolution entirely, which makes it more parallelizable.
Reducing to a single attention head costs 0.9 BLEU, and using too many heads also degrades quality.
The base model already surpasses all previously published models and ensembles at a fraction of their training cost.
The Transformer generalizes to English constituency parsing, reaching 92.7 F1 in the semi-supervised setting.

claims.text: The Transformer relies entirely on attention mechanisms and uses neither recurrence nor convolution.
On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task the model reaches 28.4 BLEU.
The big model improves on the previous best results, including ensembles, by more than 2 BLEU on English-to-German.
The big model was trained for 3.5 days on eight P100 GPUs.
The base model surpasses all previously published models and ensembles at a fraction of their training cost.
Using a single attention head costs about 0.9 BLEU compared with the best configuration.
The authors plan to extend the Transformer to modalities other than text, such as images and audio.
The Transformer replaces the recurrent layers usual in encoder-decoder architectures with multi-head self-attention.
On the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task the model reaches 31.7 BLEU.
The big model was trained for twelve days on sixty-four P100 GPUs.
Single-head attention improves BLEU by 0.9 over the best configuration.
The Transformer uses convolutional layers in place of recurrence.
The model was evaluated on the WMT 2014 English-to-Russian translation task.
The base model underperforms all previously published single models.
The authors report that the Transformer cannot be applied to constituency parsing.
Training the base model required more compute than the previous state of the art.
